_notes: The provincial meeting's common policies (E2 §2.2). The bishops of a province meet twice a year (custom, not law; verify) and now and then adopt something common. Each policy has a lean (−1 observant .. +1 progressive, 0 for the practical ones) that the province's bishops' mean reading weighs, the letter the diocesan bishop sends his priests when it comes home, and the flag the parish scenes read (metropolia:policy:<id>, the week). Numbers invented.

policies.label: A common Mass schedule
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed a common floor for Sunday Masses: no parish served by one priest is to keep more than three, and no two parishes within five miles the same hour. The schedule is to be published by Advent.
Your bishop adds that he expects the deaneries to sort it out among themselves, and that he will sort it out for any deanery that does not.

policies.label: One seminary for the province
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed to send their men to one seminary, the province's, from next autumn; the two dioceses that sent men elsewhere will stop. The faculty is to be drawn from all the dioceses.
Your bishop says the diocese will be asked for a professor, and that he has a name in mind.

policies.label: A common norm for the older form
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed a common norm for the older form of the Mass across the province, so that a family need not drive to the next diocese for it or to avoid it: the same faculties, the same conditions, the same places, published together.
Your bishop's covering note says the norm is the province's and the exceptions are his.
policies.line: the province's common norm for the older Mass

policies.label: A provincial tribunal
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed to staff one tribunal for marriage cases, at the metropolitan see, with judges lent from every diocese; the diocesan tribunals will take instruction and the first hearing only.
Your bishop says a canonist of the diocese will be asked for two days a week, and that the wait for a decision should fall by a year.

policies.label: A provincial clergy convocation
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed to a convocation of the province's priests every third year, four days at the provincial seminary, with a speaker the province chooses and the bishops in the back row.
Your bishop says attendance is expected, and that the last one was, he is told, worth the drive.

policies.label: A joint statement on immigration
letter: The bishops of the province have issued a joint statement on the treatment of immigrants in the province's cities and fields, to be read or summarised at every Mass on the coming Sunday, with a collection for the province's immigration services the Sunday after.
Your bishop's note says he signed it, and that he knows which parishes will read it and which will summarise.

policies.label: A joint statement on religious liberty
letter: The bishops of the province have issued a joint statement on religious liberty and the conscience of Catholic institutions, to be read at every Mass on the coming Sunday and printed in the bulletin.
Your bishop's note says he signed it, and that he expects it read and not summarised.
policies.line: the province's statement on religious liberty

policies.label: A common safeguarding audit
letter: The bishops of the province have agreed to one safeguarding audit for the whole province, by one firm, with one report published for all the dioceses together.
Your bishop says every parish will be visited, and that the auditors are to be given whatever they ask for.
